title: Ang 968–974: Ramkali's Bhagats
tomorrow: what happens to a pile of wrongs you can't undo?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 966: Satta and Balvand, and one light moving into a new body. Today, the Bhagats, and something you can feel in your hands.

Some people can talk, text and cook dinner all at once, and still not burn the rice. Namdev noticed people like that too. Ang 972, in paraphrase: a boy takes paper, cuts out a kite, and flies it up into the sky; he chats and jokes with his friends, and his attention stays on the string. Namdev's hymn is full of people like that, busy with their hands and steady somewhere else. Today's lesson lives in the fingers.
screen: `TALKING, TEXTING, COOKING.` → `A BOY AND A KITE.` → `HIS MIND ON THE STRING.`

segments.voice: Ramkali's last pages belong to the Bhagats, devotees whose hymns were gathered into the Granth beside the Gurus' own: Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas and Beni, each with a distinct voice. Namdev's hymn is the one you can feel in your hands. After the kite come more pictures, in paraphrase: young women carrying water pots on their heads, laughing and talking along the path, their attention on the pot. A mother busy around the house, her child in the cradle, her mind on the child. Every picture is someone in motion, holding one thread tight. The kite string tugging the fingers. The weight of the pot balanced on the crown of the head. The cradle in the corner of the eye. That's how Namdev says it is with a mind on the One: you don't stop living to do it. You keep the string in your fingers while the day goes on. And notice who's on these pages. In their own hymns, Kabir calls himself a weaver, Ravidas a leatherworker, and Namdev, tradition says, came from a family of cloth printers. The Granth gives them the same pages as the Gurus. Different hands, different trades, one string.
screen: `THE BHAGATS: FOUR VOICES.` · `THE KITE, THE POT, THE CRADLE.` · `KEEP THE STRING WHILE YOU LIVE.` · `DIFFERENT HANDS, ONE STRING.` · then, large: `THE BHAGATS.`

segments.voice: Pick one quiet thread: the feel of the breath at the tip of the nose. Let the room's sounds come and go, and thoughts too, like friends chatting on the path. Keep a fingertip of attention on the breath the whole time, the way the boy keeps his on the string.
Ang 968. Where Ramkali's Bhagats begin: Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas and Beni, and Namdev's kite on its string.
The bhagats: different hands, different trades, one string held all through a busy day. See you soon.
